title: Visualizing the way out
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you cannot sleep because of a problem, what is your mind doing?

Jose said that in this chapter the person sits on the edge of the bed, unable to sleep, with the stress going through the roof. He had survived the surges and the storms of the year, short sellers circling like vultures, and he is running out of money. What is his process in crisis mode?
A student said: he looks for an opportunity or a gap where he could refine and make more efficient, to potentially make the money he needs.

Another read from the book that he had to divorce himself from reality in order to get out of a bad situation when he thought disaster was imminent. Jose said: beautiful. What is reality for him, and what is reality for other people?

A student said: by reality I think he means what is likely to happen. Jose said: but he also pushes the boundaries of what is likely to happen. What other people consider likely isn't what he considers likely.

What is he doing mentally, when he sits up at night? A student said: he's visualizing. Jose said: I don't really like the word manifestation, so let's stick with visualization. It is more pragmatic. He is looking for a very specific situation to get him out of the trouble he's in.
Then he says: I solved it. He is going to host a day where investors will get a demonstration of how the company is building a car that drives itself.
When you cannot sleep, what are you rehearsing?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you rehearse in those hours.
Write the gap or opportunity you could look for.
Write what you consider likely, and whether you could push it.
Write the specific situation that would get you out of the problem.

check.q: What did a student say the person looks for in a crisis?
choices: An opportunity or a gap to make more efficient

check.q: What word did Jose prefer to manifestation?
What did a student say reality means in the book's phrase?

recap: Visualize a specific way out. Test what you think is likely.
